nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms, let $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ be formulas (with $n \ge 0$) and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $\Box(\gamma_1 \to \cdots \to \gamma_n \to \varphi) \to (\Box\gamma_1 \to \cdots \to \Box\gamma_n \to \Box\varphi)$ is a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Boxing an implication chain

nodes.summary: For a set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, this is the unimodal model of CSLib's modal semantics whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$, in which $M$ sees $N$ iff $\varphi \in N$ for every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $M$ iff $p \in M$.
nodes.title: The canonical model as a CSLib model

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms such that $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$. The canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ is the Kripke model whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$ (there is at least one, by Lindenbaum's lemma), in which $M$ sees $N$ iff $\varphi \in N$ for every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $M$ iff…
nodes.title: The canonical model

nodes.summary: For a set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, the worlds of the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$: the sets of formulas that are consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ and have no consistent proper superset.
nodes.title: Worlds of the canonical model

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in K.
nodes.title: Strong completeness of K

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model with reflexive and transitive accessibility relation whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in S4.
nodes.title: Strong completeness of S4

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in S5.
nodes.title: Strong completeness of S5

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model with reflexive accessibility relation whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in T.
nodes.title: Strong completeness of T

nodes.summary: For every set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, a set of formulas is consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ iff all its finite subsets are.
nodes.title: Consistency is of finite character

nodes.summary: For sets of formulas $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$, the set $\Gamma$ is consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ when $\bot$ is not deducible from $\Gamma$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Consistency relative to a normal modal logic

nodes.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in K if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over all Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Strong soundness and completeness of K

nodes.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in S4 if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over reflexive transitive Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model with reflexive and transitive accessibility relation, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Strong soundness and completeness of S4

nodes.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in S5 if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over Kripke models whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every such Kripke model, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Strong soundness and completeness of S5

nodes.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in T if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over reflexive Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model with reflexive accessibility relation, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Strong soundness and completeness of T

nodes.summary:
For every set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms and every modal formula $\psi$, the formula $\Box\psi 	o \Box
eg
eg\psi$ is a theorem of the normal modal logic $K \oplus \Lambda$, where $
eg\chi$ abbreviates $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Double-negation introduction under a box

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of K if and only if $\varphi$ is valid, that is, true at every world, in every Kripke model whose worlds live in the universe of the atoms.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of K

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language over a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of K if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic K over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model with worlds $W$.
nodes.title: Completeness for CSLib's K

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms, and let $S$ be a set of CSLib unimodal models whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$. If $S$ contains the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$, viewed as a CSLib model, and a CSLib proposition $\varphi$ holds at every world of every model in $S$, then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of…
nodes.title: Validity in a class containing the canonical model gives derivability

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language over a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of S4 if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic S4 over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model with worlds $W$ whose accessibility relation is…
nodes.title: Completeness for CSLib's S4

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language over a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of S5 if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic S5 over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model with worlds $W$ whose accessibility relation…
nodes.title: Completeness for CSLib's S5

nodes.summary: For a CSLib unimodal proposition $\varphi$, the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system T if and only if, for every type of worlds in the universe of the atoms, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic T over that type, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive.
nodes.title: Completeness for CSLib's T

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S4 if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of S4

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S5 if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of S5

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of T if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of T

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$. Every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas that is consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ is contained in a set $M$ of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for normal modal logics

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, $M$ a canonical world, that is, a set of modal formulas maximal among the sets consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, and $\varphi$ a modal formula. If $\Box\varphi \notin M$, then there is a canonical world $N$ with $\varphi \notin N$ that is accessible from $M$ in the…
nodes.title: Existence lemma

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas, $\varphi$ a modal formula and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ a list of modal formulas. If $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n\}$ in the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, then $\gamma_1 \to (\gamma_2 \to \cdots \to (\gamma_n \to \varphi) \cdots)$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in the same logic.
nodes.title: Discharging a list of hypotheses

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a class of Kripke models, given as a predicate on models. A set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas locally entails a formula $\varphi$ over $C$ when, for every Kripke model $M$ in $C$ whose type of worlds lies in the universe of the atoms and every world $w$ of $M$, if every formula of $\Gamma$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$, then $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Local semantic consequence over a class of Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system K, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic K: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type.
nodes.title: Soundness for CSLib's K

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a class of CSLib unimodal models on a type of worlds and $\varphi$ a CSLib unimodal proposition. Suppose that, if the type of worlds is nonempty, the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is valid in the Kripke model of every model in $S$. Then $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic of $S$: it holds at every world of every model in $S$.
nodes.title: Validity of the translation gives membership in CSLib's logic

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $M$ a set of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$. Every formula that is a local consequence of $M$ in that logic belongs to $M$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets of modal formulas are deductively closed

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $M$ a set of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, and $\varphi$ and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ modal formulas. If $\gamma_1 \to (\gamma_2 \to \cdots \to (\gamma_n \to \varphi) \cdots) \in M$ and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n \in M$, then $\varphi \in M$.
nodes.title: Iterated modus ponens in maximal consistent sets

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system S4, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic S4: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive.
nodes.title: Soundness for CSLib's S4

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system S5, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic S5: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation $R$ is reflexive, transitive and Euclidean ($R(w, u)$ and $R(w, v)$ imply $R(u, v)$).
nodes.title: Soundness for CSLib's S5

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system T, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic T: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive.
nodes.title: Soundness for CSLib's T

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas such that $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$, let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\varphi$ holds at every world of the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds, then $\Gamma$ deduces $\varphi$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Completeness relative to the canonical model

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\varphi$ belongs to every maximal $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent set that contains $\Gamma$, then $\Gamma$ deduces $\varphi$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Deducibility from maximal consistent extensions

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a Kripke model on a nonempty type of worlds. Converting $k$ to a CSLib unimodal model and converting that model back to a Kripke model gives $k$.
nodes.title: Kripke to CSLib and back is the identity

nodes.summary: For a CSLib unimodal model $m$ on a nonempty type of worlds, the associated Kripke model has the same worlds, the binary accessibility relation of $m$ as its accessibility relation, and the valuation of $m$ as its valuation.
nodes.title: Kripke model of a CSLib model

nodes.summary: CSLib's unimodal propositions are translated into modal formulas in the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis by recursion, writing $\varphi'$ for the translation of $\varphi$: an atom $p$ goes to $p$, falsehood to $\bot$, $\neg\varphi$ to $\varphi' \to \bot$, $\varphi \lor \psi$ to $(\varphi' \to \bot) \to \psi'$, and the diamond (the unimodal triangle) applied to $\varphi$ goes to $\Diamond\varphi'$, that is, to…
nodes.title: Translation of CSLib's modal propositions

nodes.summary: For a set $\Lambda$ of modal formulas and maximal $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent sets $M$ and $N$ (worlds of the canonical model), $M$ is related to $N$ iff every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$ belongs to $N$.
nodes.title: The canonical accessibility relation

nodes.summary: For every K-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for K

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $C$ a class of Kripke models whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, such that $C$ contains the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ whenever $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$. Then every $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent set $\Gamma$ of formulas is satisfiable in $C$: some model in $C$ has a world at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence from the canonical model

nodes.summary: For every S4-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a reflexive transitive Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for S4

nodes.summary: For every S5-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence and whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for S5

nodes.summary: For every T-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a reflexive Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for T

nodes.summary: A formula holds at a world of the canonical model iff it belongs to it.
nodes.title: Truth lemma

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a CSLib unimodal model on a nonempty type of worlds, $w$ a world and $\varphi$ a CSLib unimodal proposition. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis holds at $w$ in the Kripke model of $m$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ in $m$.
nodes.title: The translation preserves satisfaction

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a Kripke model, $w$ a world and $\varphi$ a modal formula in the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis. Then $\varphi$ holds at $w$ in $k$ if and only if its translation into a CSLib unimodal proposition holds at $w$ in the CSLib model associated with $k$.
nodes.title: The reverse translation preserves satisfaction

nodes.summary: For a nonempty type of worlds $W$, converting a CSLib unimodal model $m$ on $W$ into a Kripke model and then back into a CSLib unimodal model returns $m$: a unimodal frame is determined by its binary accessibility relation.
nodes.title: Round trip from CSLib models through Kripke models

nodes.summary: A Kripke model $k$ on worlds $W$ gives the CSLib unimodal model on $W$ whose frame is the unimodal frame built from the accessibility relation of $k$ and whose valuation is the valuation of $k$.
nodes.title: The CSLib unimodal model of a Kripke model

nodes.summary:
Each modal formula built from atoms, $ ot$, $	o$ and $\Box$ is translated into a CSLib unimodal proposition by recursion: an atom $p$ goes to the atom $p$, $ ot$ goes to false, $\varphi 	o \psi$ goes to $
eg\varphi' \lor \psi'$, and $\Box\varphi$ goes to $
eg\Diamond
eg\varphi'$, where $\varphi'$ and $\psi'$ are the translations of $\varphi$ and $\psi$ and $\Diamond$ is the possibility operator of CSLib's…
nodes.title: Translation of modal formulas into CSLib propositions

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is valid in a Kripke model $k$ (true at every world of $k$) if and only if its translation into a CSLib unimodal proposition is satisfied at every world of the CSLib unimodal model associated with $k$.
nodes.title: Validity agrees with its CSLib translation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
